Mesillat Yesharim 19:50: And whoever diminishes this where he could have increased it is nothing but a sinner. This is what the prophet Malachi rebukes Israel concerning, in the word of the Lord (Malachi 1:8): "And when you offer the blind for sacrifice, is it not evil? And when you offer the lame and sick, is it not evil? Offer it now to your governor; will he be pleased with you, or accept your face?"
Mesillat Yesharim 19:51: However, our Sages, of blessed memory, warned us to conduct ourselves the opposite way in service, and they said (Sukkah 50a): regarding water that was left uncovered, that one may not strain it through a strainer for use in a libation, for the reasoning is: perhaps this is said for an ordinary person — but for the Most High, is it said?! Does He not have the verse "offer it now to your governor"?!
Mesillat Yesharim 19:52: See now what deficiency there is in strained water — it is already permitted to an ordinary person, and even so it is forbidden for the Most High, because it is not the way of honor.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:53: And they further said in the Sifrei (Deuteronomy 12:11): "and all your choice votive offerings" — that is, one should bring only from the choicest.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:54: And we have already found the case of Cain and Abel: Abel brought from the firstborn of his flock and from their fattest parts, while Cain brought from the inferior produce of the ground, as our Sages, of blessed memory, explained; and what came of it? (Genesis 4:4-5): "And the Lord had regard for Abel and for his offering, but for Cain and for his offering He had no regard."
Mesillat Yesharim 19:55: And it says (Malachi 1:14): "But cursed be the deceiver who has a male in his flock, and vows and sacrifices to the Lord a blemished thing; for I am a great King."
Mesillat Yesharim 19:56: And our Sages, of blessed memory, warned us in many statements that commandments should not be treated as contemptible by us, and they have already said (Shabbat 14a; Megillah 32a): whoever holds a Torah scroll naked, without its wrapping, will be buried naked, because of the disgrace of the commandment.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:57: And the order of the bringing of the first fruits should be before our eyes as an example of how commandments are to be beautified, for so we learned (Bikkurim 3): the ox goes before them with its horns overlaid with gold and a wreath of olive leaves upon its head, etc. It further states there: the rich would bring their first fruits in baskets of gold, and the poor in baskets of peeled willow, etc. It further states there: there are three measures in the first fruits: first fruits, an addition to the first fruits, and the adornment of the first fruits, etc. Behold, then, how clearly it teaches us how much we ought to add beyond the essential body of a commandment in order to beautify it, and from this we may learn regarding all the other commandments of the Torah.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:58: And they said (Shabbat 10a): Rava would put on his stockings and pray, saying (Amos 4:12): "Prepare to meet your God, O Israel."
Mesillat Yesharim 19:59: Our Sages, of blessed memory, further said (Bereishit Rabbah 65): on the verse "the precious garments of Esau her son" (Genesis 27:15) — Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said: I served my father, etc., but Esau, when he served his father, would serve him only in royal garments.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:60: Now, if this is so with flesh and blood, how much more so with the King of kings of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He — whoever stands before Him to pray should surely put on garments of honor, and sit before Him as one who sits before a great king.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:61: And included in this is the honor of Sabbaths and festivals, for whoever increases in honoring them certainly gives satisfaction to his Maker, for so He commanded us: "and you shall honor it" (Isaiah 58:13).
Mesillat Yesharim 19:62: And since it has already become clear to us that honoring it is a commandment, there are many kinds of honor; but the general rule is that we must do every act that displays importance for the Sabbath.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:63: Therefore the early Sages would occupy themselves with the preparations for the Sabbath, each one in his own way (Shabbat 119a): Rabbi Abbahu would sit on an ivory stool and fan the fire; Rav Safra would singe the head of an animal for the meal; Rava would salt the shibuta fish; Rav Huna would light the lamp; Rav Pappa would twist the wick; Rav Chisda would cut the beets; Rabbah and Rav Yosef would chop wood; Rav Nachman would carry things on his shoulder, going in and out with the load on his shoulder, saying: if Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi were to visit me, would I not carry things on my shoulder before them?
Mesillat Yesharim 19:64: And you will see the analogy Rav Nachman drew, from which we can learn a lesson, for he reflected on what he himself would do, in his own way, for a person whom he wished to honor, and did the very same for the Sabbath.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:65: And concerning this it is said (Berachot 17a): a person should always be shrewd in fear of Heaven — to know and reflect, deriving one matter from another, and to devise new inventions for giving satisfaction to his Maker in every way possible,
Mesillat Yesharim 19:66: showing that we recognize the greatness of His majesty over us — so that whatever is associated with Him will be greatly honored by us; and since He, blessed be He, in His great goodness, notwithstanding all our lowliness, wished, in His humility, to grant us honor and to entrust to us the words of His holiness, let us at least honor them with all our strength, and show the preciousness they hold for us.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:67: And you will see that this is the true fear — the fear of His grandeur which we mentioned, upon which depends the honor that draws near to the endearment of love, as I will write further, with the help of Heaven — unlike the fear of punishment, which is not the essential fear, and from which the virtues of these traits do not follow.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:68: Let us return to the matter of the Sabbath. Behold, they said (Shabbat 119a): Rav Anan would wear a black garment, that is, he would wear a black garment on the eve of the Sabbath, so that the honor of the Sabbath would be more noticeable when he put on beautiful garments for it.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:69: It follows that not only the preparation for the Sabbath is included in its honor, but even the absence beforehand by which the presence of the honor is more discerned is also included in the commandment; and so they forbade setting a fixed meal on the eve of the Sabbath, because of the honor of the Sabbath, and so with all similar things.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:70: And also included in fear is the honoring of the Torah and its students, and we learned explicitly (Avot 4:6): whoever honors the Torah is himself honored by his fellow creatures.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:71: And they said, of blessed memory (Sanhedrin 102b): Rabbi Yochanan said, why did Ahab merit to reign for twenty-two years? Because he honored the Torah, which was given in twenty-two letters, as it is said, "and he sent messengers to Ahab, etc." (I Kings 20:2-9) — "but this thing I cannot do."
Mesillat Yesharim 19:72: And they said, of blessed memory (Berachot 18a): if he was traveling from place to place with a Torah scroll with him, he should not place it in a sack and put it on a donkey and ride upon it, but rather he should hold it in his lap, etc.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:73: And they further forbade (Moed Katan 25a) sitting on a bed upon which a Torah scroll rests. And they likewise said (Eruvin 98a): sacred writings may not be thrown, and even halachot and aggadot may not be thrown. And they forbade (Megillah 27a) placing the Prophets and the Writings on top of the Five Books of Moses. These are matters that our Sages, of blessed memory, forbade for the entire congregation of Israel; but the pious person should learn from these and add to them many more, for the honor of the Name of the Lord his God.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:74: And included in this is the cleanliness and purity required for words of Torah — not to engage with it even in thought in filthy places, nor with unclean hands; and our Sages, of blessed memory, gave many warnings about this in numerous places.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:75: And regarding those who study Torah, Scripture says explicitly: "you shall rise up before the hoary head, and honor the face of the old man" (Leviticus 19:32), and from this we derive every kind of honor that can possibly be shown to them, which it is certainly proper for the pious person to do.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:76: And they have already said, of blessed memory (Ketubot 103b): "and he honors those who fear the Lord" (Psalms 15:4) — this refers to Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, who, whenever he saw a Torah scholar, would rise from his throne and embrace him and kiss him and say to him: My teacher, my teacher, my master, my master.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:77: And Rabbi Zeira, when he was weak from his studies, would place himself at the entrance of the study hall, in order to perform the mitzvah of rising before Torah scholars when they passed (Berachot 28a).
Mesillat Yesharim 19:78: All these are matters which we already see that the Creator, blessed be His Name, desires, and He has revealed His supernal will concerning them.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:79: And since this is so, whoever wishes to give satisfaction to his Maker will proceed in this manner, adding ever more insight into his own strategies for this, and doing what is upright before Him, blessed be His Name.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:80: And included in this as well is the honor of the synagogue and the study hall, for it is not enough merely not to treat them with levity, but rather one should treat them with every kind of honor and reverence in all his conduct and all his actions, and whatever he would not do in the palace of a great king, he should not do in them.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:81: Let us now speak of the matter of love; its branches are three: joy, cleaving, and zealousness.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:82: Now, the matter of love is that a person should truly long and yearn for closeness to Him, blessed be He, and pursue His holiness, just as a man pursues, with intense longing, something precious to him — to the point that mentioning His Name, blessed be He, and speaking of His praises, and occupying himself with the words of His Torah and His divinity, blessed be He, become for him actual delight and pleasure, like one who loves the wife of his youth or his only son with a powerful love, so that even mere speech of them is for him contentment and delight — in the vein of the verse (Jeremiah 31:19): "for as often as I speak of him, I remember him still."
Mesillat Yesharim 19:83: And behold, it is certain that whoever loves his Creator with a true love will not abandon his service for any reason in the world, unless he is truly under duress.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:84: And he will not need persuasion or enticement toward the service, but rather, on the contrary, his own heart will carry him and rush him toward it, unless some great obstacle holds him back.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:85: Behold, this is the beloved trait which the early pious ones, the holy ones on high, merited, as King David, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 42:2-3): "As the deer longs for the water brooks, so my soul longs for You, O God; my soul thirsts for God, for the living God; when shall I come, etc." And it says (ibid. 84:3): "My soul yearns, indeed, it faints, for the courts of the Lord, etc." (ibid. 63:2): "My soul thirsts for You, my flesh longs for You, etc." All this out of the force of the longing he felt for Him, blessed be He.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:86: In the vein of what the prophet said (Isaiah 26:8): "to Your Name and to Your remembrance is the desire of the soul," and it says: "my soul has desired You in the night, indeed my spirit within me seeks You earnestly." And David himself says (Psalms 63:7): "if I remembered You upon my bed, I meditate on You in the night watches" — explaining the delight and pleasure he had in speaking of Him and of His praises, blessed be His Name; and he says (ibid. 119:47): "and I will delight myself in Your commandments, which I have loved," and he said (ibid.): "Your testimonies also are my delight, etc."
Mesillat Yesharim 19:87: And behold, this love must certainly not be a love dependent on some external thing — that is, that he should love the Creator, blessed be He, because He does good to him, enriches him, and makes him prosperous — but rather like the love of a son for his father, which is a truly natural love, which his own nature compels and forces upon him, as Scripture says (Deuteronomy 32:6): "Is He not your Father who acquired you?"
Mesillat Yesharim 19:88: And the test of this love comes at a time of distress and trouble, and so they said, of blessed memory (ibid. 6:5): "and you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul" — even if He takes your soul — "and with all your might" — with all your money.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:89: However, so that troubles and distresses should not become an obstacle and a hindrance to love, a person should give himself two answers: one of them applies equally to every soul, and the second is for the wise, possessors of deeper understanding.
